newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini wants golden shares to be temporary.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini wants golden shares to be temporary.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Saturday he thought golden shares in privatised companies were useful, but should only be temporary.
"I don't think a golden share is a backwards step as far as privatisation is concerned but I do think it should be a temporary solution," he told reporters at an Anglo-Italian seminar in Venice.
Dini, a former economist and central banker, stressed that he was expressing personal views.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said last month that the government favoured keeping a golden share after the merger of telecommunications holding Stet with its fixed-line operator Telecom Italia, due later this year.
Stet said on Friday it would propose giving "special powers" to the Treasury ahead of the planned privatisation.
The move indicated that the government would keep a golden share in the telecom holding, enabling the Treasury to dictate policy after it gave up its majority stake.

Italy's Constitutional Court ruled in January to allow a proposed referendum seeking to abolish the use of golden shares, which give the Treasury special powers in privatised companies deemed to be of public interest. A referendum is due to be held on the issue.
The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support gives Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government a majority in parliament, has opposed the Stet sell-off.

Some legislation still has to be approved by parliament before the sell-off can go ahead and key members of the centre-left coalition have held lengthy meetings with Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti this week.
Dini was optimistic. "I think the obstacles posed by Communist Refoundation have been overcome," he said.
